title: Event delegation
learningObjectives: Explain event delegation and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Event delegation attaches one listener to a common ancestor and uses event.target or closest() to identify which descendant triggered the event. It relies on event bubbling and is useful for dynamic lists where children are added or removed.
understand.whyItMatters: Delegation reduces the number of listeners and supports elements created after initial page load. The handler must verify that the matched element belongs to the intended container.
understand.analogy: Instead of assigning a guard to every door, one attendant watches the shared entrance and identifies which door the visitor came from.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: One listener handles buttons inside the courses container, including buttons added later. The containment check prevents matching an element outside the container.

examples.explanation: One listener handles buttons inside the courses container, including buttons added later. The containment check prevents matching an element outside the container.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Build a dynamic list that adds course buttons. Use one parent listener to handle all button clicks safely.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: What makes event delegation work for many click events?
options: Bubbling events reaching a shared ancestor
questions.answer: Bubbling events reaching a shared ancestor
questions.explanation: Delegation relies on events bubbling to a common ancestor that owns the listener.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
